prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which bifunctional small molecules bring a chosen protein and an E3 ubiquitin ligase together so that the cell destroys it, from the PROTAC concept to its structure-guided chemical design.

statement.case_for: I have changed my preferred configuration from B006 (nitrogenase) to B018 (targeted protein degradation), as a single achievement limited to the PROTAC and induced-proximity strand. The reason is the exchange itself. In round 1 I defended a structure-only nitrogenase citation, but Chabes, Zou and Sparr each pressed the same point from different sides: the resting-state cofactor is known, whereas the N2 binding site and the catalytic intermediates are not, and the cryo-EM turnover states have not been independently reproduced. A citation that avoids mechanism is defensible, but it splits credit among five people and is the weakest of the options for a physical-mechanism prize. B018 meets the criterion I care about: induced proximity is a new principle, and it is quantitatively testable. Ternary-complex cooperativity, the crystal structure of a PROTAC-induced VHL-target complex, and degradation kinetics can all be measured, and the field has been reproduced by many independent groups over two decades. Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated the heterobifunctional degrader in 2001. Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and his ternary-complex structural and biophysical work turned a proof of principle into a general chemical series, which is the physical-chemistry content I would want a citation to rest on. I name the PROTAC strand alone, because the cereblon and glue strand (Handa, Ito) has different discoverers and a different mechanism and, as I said in round 1, a combined citation forces an arbitrary split.
statement.case_against: No degrader drug is approved, and I will not pretend that the medical consequences are delivered. This is the main risk, and it is why nitrogenase and Pd-catalysed C-N coupling remain my alternatives, since both are more mature. The three-name cap also omits Sakamoto, Gray, Handa, Ito and Kim, and the choice of Ciulli over Handa as the third name is a judgement about which part of the field a citation should cover, not a neutral fact. Whether PROTAC design is new chemistry or medicinal-chemistry optimisation of a ligand-linker-ligand scaffold (Somfai's concern) is not fully answered by my argument; I rely on the measured cooperativity and structural evidence, and the expert reports should confirm it.

responses.point: Chabes judged nitrogenase premature because the mechanism is open and the cryo-EM turnover states need independent reproduction, and he proposes Crews and Deshaies alone for B018 beside base editing.
responses.response: In round 1 I argued that a closed mechanism is not required for a prize. I still hold that as a principle, but your point about independent reproduction of the turnover states is correct, and with the substrate-binding site open the citation would have to be limited to structure and would spread over five people. That is why I moved. I agree with you that Crews and Deshaies are the core of B018. I differ on the pairing with base editing: I would rather the committee give one well-supported achievement than add a second part whose clinical record and separation from the 2020 prize are still debated.

responses.point: Aqvist holds B018 as the whole prize with Crews, Deshaies and Handa and is open to swapping Handa for Ciulli if the committee wants a single PROTAC-concept citation.
responses.response: I accept your framing that the quantitative chemistry is the strength of B018, and I take up your offer: I propose Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. Handa's identification of cereblon explains why thalidomide-type drugs work, and I regard it as a distinct and important achievement, but it is a different molecular mechanism from the heterobifunctional design. Putting both in one citation is the arbitrary split I warned against in round 1. If a majority wants the glue strand included, I would want that argued as its own part and not folded into this one, and I would then ask for the expert report on the cereblon work.

responses.point: Zou asked what has actually been determined for nitrogenase, and argued that a mechanism citation would run ahead of the evidence while a structure-only citation would split credit among Rees, Einsle, Dean, Ribbe and Seefeldt.
responses.response: That is a fair statement of the problem, and it is the main reason I no longer prefer B006. I keep it as my first alternative, since the cofactor structure with its carbide is a real achievement. On your own candidate, C-N coupling, I accept the clean Buchwald and Hartwig attribution and the long record of confirmation. My remaining question is the one you and Somfai were asked: after 2010, what is the principle that goes beyond ligand optimisation within the same Pd(0)/Pd(II) manifold? Without a clear answer from the expert reports I will not put B002 first, though I would not oppose it.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, supports base editing with Liu alone together with Crews and Deshaies for PROTACs, and asks whether Liu-only is defensible given the Nishida and Kondo claim.
responses.response: I agree with you on Crews and Deshaies as the origin of the PROTAC concept. On B029 I still find the Liu-centred attribution the cleanest on the shortlist, but I cannot judge from the files whether the Target-AID priority claim is secondary, and I want the expert report on it before I support a Liu-only part. For the question on an evidence threshold for B018: I do not make approval of a drug a precondition, because the committee has honoured principles before clinical outcomes, but I would want independent confirmation of the ternary-complex mechanism, which exists, and I would change my ranking if the degrader clinical data showed an unexpected mechanistic failure.

responses.point: Somfai asks whether PROTAC design is new chemistry or medicinal-chemistry optimisation, and ranks Buchwald and Hartwig first, with Liu as a second part.
responses.response: The question is the right one for B018. My answer is that the new content is not the compound class but the principle, a small molecule that induces a ternary complex whose cooperativity can be measured and designed, so that the cell's own ligase does the chemistry of destruction. That is why I include Ciulli, whose structures and biophysics put the cooperativity on a quantitative footing. I accept that this is a judgement, and the expert report should test it. I do not share your view that base editing should be the second part of a prize; I consider it too close to the 2020 prize and too early clinically to carry a part in a two-part prize.

responses.point: Sparr holds B018 as the whole prize with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, concedes that no degrader is approved, and sees the PROTAC and glue strands as possibly two achievements.
responses.response: We now share the same single-achievement structure, and you are right that the two strands may be two achievements. I would handle that by restricting this prize to the PROTAC and induced-proximity strand, with Handa's cereblon work left outside the citation, and not by stretching one citation across both. I note that you moved away from phase separation on maturity grounds, and I agree with that, since the distinction between demixing and other assemblies in living cells is not settled.

uncertainties: Whether Ciulli or Handa is the right third name, and whether the committee can accept a PROTAC-only citation that leaves the cereblon glue strand outside.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader drug makes B018 premature relative to B002 or B006, and what the expert reports say about the ternary-complex evidence.
Whether PROTAC design counts as new chemical principle or as optimisation, and whether Sakamoto's early contribution should displace one of the three names.
Whether the committee will want a structure-based nitrogenase prize in a later cycle, once the intermediates are better established.
statement.conflict_note: I am a colleague of Xiaodong Zou at Stockholm University, which is a general institutional connection and not a conflict for any shortlisted candidate. I have no collaboration or personal tie to Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli or any other credited name, so I disclose no specific conflict and see no recusal need. My own field of respiratory enzymes is adjacent to nitrogenase (B006), which is now only an alternative; this is a subject-matter proximity and not a conflict.
